title: Enums and Literal Types
description: Learn to model fixed value sets with enums and string/numeric literal types.

data.text: Sometimes a value can only be one of a few specific options. Enums and literal types give these fixed value sets a name, making your code clearer and catching invalid values at compile time.

data.title: Numeric Enum
String Enum

data.text: Literal types describe exactly one value. Combined with union types they create a lightweight alternative to enums.

data.title: Literal Types
data.content: String and numeric literals as types

cards.title: Enums
cards.description: A named collection of constant values that TypeScript compiles to a real runtime object.

cards.title: Literal Unions
cards.description: A type made of exact string or number values. No runtime object is created.

data.title: When to Use Which
data.text: Use enums when you need a named, runtime-inspectable set of values. Use literal unions when you only need compile-time checking and want zero runtime cost.

data.title: Const Enum
data.content: Const enums are inlined at compile time

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: String enums are safer than numeric ones
Use const enums for performance-critical code
data.takeaway: Enums and literal types help you model a fixed set of valid values.
